title: Grateful Dead Live at Stanley Theatre on 1972-09-26
lineage: SBD Reel> unknown dat gens> digital noise reduction> 3dat gens> za/248-41

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a fiery ’72 show highlighted by a smoking Truckin > Other One > Baby Blue sequence and a monster He's Gone.
ai_review.review: The performance shines with a blazing second‑set jam from Truckin through The Other One into It’s All Over Now Baby Blue, plus a legendary He's Gone that many reviewers call the best ever.  The soundboard recording is remarkably clear – almost studio quality – though a few minutes of the Truckin/Other One jam are missing due to a tape change.  Overall the energy is high and the band delivers tight, inspired playing.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently strong praise for both musical performance (standout jams, high energy) and recording clarity; only one mixed review lowers the average slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix with crisp vocals and guitars; piano sits low in the blend but is audible.  A tape‑change removed several minutes of the Truckin > Other One jam, leaving a noticeable gap.

standout_songs: Truckin > Other One > It's All Over Now Baby Blue
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds solidly with Me & My Uncle and a powerful He's Gone; the second set erupts into a monster jam chain (Truckin → Other One → Baby Blue) and closes on a high note with Johnny B. Goode.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone is described as crisp and clear; he delivers an inspired pedal‑steel lead around 9:40 and a soulful strum/humming on Baby Blue, though some reviewers note occasional out‑of‑tune moments.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work is highlighted as standout throughout; a missing bass solo before The Other One is lamented, but his jam in the latter part of the sequence receives high praise.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s rhythm guitar and vocal contributions are noted as solid; one reviewer confirms he can “play rhythm guitar” effectively during this show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano is low in the mix but still audible, adding texture to songs like Bird Song; overall keyboard presence is felt despite the reduced level.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is called a standout element throughout the performance.
